messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: CUDA_MEMORY_PRESSURE detected on pool=dedicated-a. 6/8 GPUs >92% memory, kvcache evictions spiking, request failures increasing. paging:PD-7892

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Incident PD-7892 triggered -> paging alice_oncall (1/2)

alice_oncall: acked. I'm up, looking. any customer-facing impact yet? :eyes:

eva_support: seeing elevated 5xx errors for a few customers (org: acme-inc, org: beta-analytics). Support ticket volumes rising. ETA from monitoring ~3m ago.

alice_oncall: thanks. ben_runtime can you confirm whether this is kvcache growth or a kernel alloc pattern?

ben_runtime: jumping in. initial glance: mem usage jumps correlate with a canary deploy 10m ago that increased default context window for some routes. suspect KV cache retention + large batch concurrency.

charlie_infra: on infra side, nodes in pool dedicated-a showing GPU mem fragmentation. I have one node with repeated MIG context OOM logs.

alice_oncall: can you paste recent node logs?

charlie_infra: logs clipped below:
```
kubectl -n runtime logs node-runtime-12 -c gpu-driver | tail -n 80
[2026-03-14T08:14:02Z] cuda: alloc failed: out of memory (requested 512MB)
[2026-03-14T08:14:03Z] kvcache: insert failed, evicting oldest entries
[2026-03-14T08:14:05Z] scheduler: preempting small jobs to free 2 GPUs
```

ben_runtime: nvidia-smi snapshot from the node:
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 520.61.05    Driver Version: 520.61.05    CUDA Version: 12.1 |
| GPU  Name        Memory-Usage  Memory-Total  Util  
| 0   A100-SXM4       49.8GiB/80GiB    98%
| 1   A100-SXM4       50.1GiB/80GiB    97%
| ...
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

ben_runtime: kvcache evictions aren't keeping up with allocation pace. We see large pinned KV entries (long context requests) causing retained memory.

dana_sre: is autoshedder kicking in? I see several shed actions but not enough.

alice_oncall: mitigation plan: 1) reduce canary concurrency -> roll back changed flag; 2) temporarily enable aggressive kvcache ttl and drop large-context slot allocations; 3) preempt largest-running jobs on affected nodes; 4) notify customers in flight. Who can run rollbacks?

ben_runtime: I can flip the feature flag for the canary. Doing that now.

ben_runtime: flipped feature flag for context-window increase. rolling canary rollback initiated.

pagerduty-bot: PD-7892 acknowledged by alice_oncall

charlie_infra: preempting top 3 jobs on node-runtime-12 -> running drain script now:
```
./scripts/preempt-large.sh node-runtime-12 --grace 30s
```

alice_oncall: enabling aggressive kvcache TTL (ttl=30s) on pool dedicated-a. That will flush old KV but may increase latency for long-context calls.

ben_runtime: TTL applied via config -> /configs/pool/dedicated-a/kvcache: ttl 30s. Observability: evictions rate up, memory trending down on nodes.

charlie_infra: node-runtime-12 GPU mem dropped to ~70% on GPUs after preempt/ttl. scheduling backlog cleared.

eva_support: still seeing elevated errors but trending down. I'll draft a status note for affected customers (acme-inc, beta-analytics) — minimal data lost, requests retried by client ok.

frank_pm: please add customers list + estimated time window so I can brief AE.

alice_oncall: window: 08:12:00 - 08:22:00 UTC. Affected reqs ~2-6% of traffic to dedicated-a. Primary cause: canary feature + large-context concurrency.

ben_runtime: follow-up: we'll land an auto-shedder tweak to deprioritize >32k token jobs on this pool and add a soft limit to KV entries per session. Will propose patch in 1-2 hours.

dana_sre: raising mitigation: add node taint to prevent scheduling new long-context jobs until stable. Applying taint:dedicated-a:NoLongContext=true

charlie_infra: taint applied. New pods with label long-context won't land.

alice_oncall: good. folks - summary actions: rollback canary (done), ttl 30s applied (done), preempted big jobs (done), taint applied (done), support notified (eva to send).

eva_support: status message drafted and sent to affected customers, support tickets linked.

ben_runtime: telemetry shows memory back to baseline after 6m. I'll keep watch and schedule a follow-up roll forward with safer limits.

alice_oncall: closing PD-7892 for now but leaving thread open for postmortem. great coordination. :clap:

pagerduty-bot: PD-7892 resolved by alice_oncall

frank_pm: request postmortem with timeline and proposed guardrails (auto-shedder rules + pre-deploy load tests). I'll coordinate with product and SEs.

alice_oncall: noted. I'll open the incident doc and assign owners. thanks everyone.
